taxonomyNote: NatureServe lists the species as Crawfish Frog (L. areolatus) without a northern/southern split; Animal Diversity Web recognises a northern subspecies (L. a. circulosa). NatureServe also notes competing generic arrangements for American ranids.
fieldMarks: Stubby frog with dorsolateral ridges and dark rounded dorsal spots with light borders; throat and belly mostly unspotted.
Usually 5.7-7.5 cm snout-vent (up to 9.2 cm per ADW); yellow on the groin and thigh; males may show yellow on the dorsolateral ridges.
Call: low-pitched snore-like 'wurr-r-r-up' audible about 800 m away.
behavior: Lives in crayfish or rodent burrows; sits at the burrow mouth or on its platform to feed and retreats headfirst.
Migrates up to several hundred metres, occasionally a mile or more, between burrow and breeding pools; inactive in winter in the north.
Males call at night in choruses in warm weather; eats moths, ants, spiders, grasshoppers, beetles and crickets.
habitat: Moist meadows, pastures, flood plains and tall-grass prairie where crayfish burrows exist; breeds in flooded fields, ditches, farm ponds, usually fishless temporary water.
range: Northern Mississippi, northern Louisiana and eastern Texas north through Oklahoma, Arkansas, western Tennessee and Kentucky to eastern Kansas, southern Illinois and Indiana (formerly southern Iowa).

lookalikes.name: Gopher frog
lookalikes.howToTell: Gopher frog (Rana capito) has a pigmented belly and lacks the light borders around the dark dorsal spots.
